title: UK CPI — December 2026 consumer price inflation (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the print that hands the duty-timing rise back and the last clean read before a triple-notched January index
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukdecember2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 42,028 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Consumer price inflation, UK: December 2026', 'Release date: 20 January 2027 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', and carries the UK Statistics Authority accredited-official-statistics kitemark. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:) has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap every sibling UK CPI entry was filed under. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2026-12-16, 2026-09-09; researched and made canonical by its own lane 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/uk-cpi-2027-01-20.from-uk-cpi-2026-12-16.json, which was read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. The proposer's framing — that this print is the mirror of 2026-12-16 and gives back what duty timing lends it — is CONFIRMED and quantified, and the initial research adds three things the proposal did not have. FIRST, THE BASE IS HARD ON ITS OWN TERMS, NOT ONLY IN DIVISION 02: the all-items December 2025 m/m was +0.430% (ONS D7BT 139.5 -> 140.1, fetched direct 2026-09-09), the THIRD-HIGHEST of thirteen Decembers against a 13-year mean of +0.281%. For this print's annual rate to RISE, December 2026 must beat +0.430% m/m — a bar only two of the other twelve Decembers in the window cleared (2016 +0.493%, 2021 +0.524%) — in a year whose duty uprating has already been taken in November. SECOND, THE DUTY SIGNATURE SPLITS 3-FOR-3 IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: division 02 (D7BV) printed NEGATIVE m/m in December in every late-October-Budget year (2018 -1.067%, 2021 -0.816%, 2024 -0.200%) and POSITIVE in every year the uprating landed in the December index (2017 +0.564%, 2023 +1.352%, 2025 +1.025%). Against the +1.025% base and the 2026 weight of 37.1650/1000 (CHZS), the unwind is -0.046 to -0.078pp on the annual rate, central -0.064pp — which nets to +0.006pp against the uk-cpi-2026-12-16 lane's +0.070pp November push, the round trip a pure timing shift must produce. Food adds -0.041pp (2026's Feb-Jul run rate is +0.012%/month against a Dec-2025 base of +0.840%; the December seasonal excess over a year's own run rate averages +0.456pp across 2016-2025); fixed-tariff energy drift offsets ~+0.010pp. ATTRIBUTABLE -0.06 TO -0.13pp, CENTRAL ~-0.10pp; the memo of full reversion to the 13-year December mean is -0.149pp and corroborates rather than bounds it. THIRD, THE PLACEMENT IS THE INVERSE OF ITS SIBLING'S: the Bank of England's own upcoming-MPC-dates page (fetched direct 2026-09-09) lists 'Thursday 4 February' 2027 under '2027 provisional dates' as 'February MPC Summary and minutes and February Monetary Policy Report'. By the BoE's published convention (announcement one day after the meeting ends) that is a meeting ending 3 February, so this print lands FIFTEEN DAYS AHEAD OF A FORECAST ROUND — not inside a voting morning — and it is the ONLY CPI print between the 2026-12-17 and 2027-02-04 announcements. It is therefore the datum that adjudicates the sibling ledger's central claim (a higher November headline is duty timing, not reacceleration) with the MPR round two weeks away. AND IT IS THE LAST CLEAN INDEX OF THE RUN: the 1 January 2027 fuel duty step (uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01), the January-March Ofgem cap step (ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25), the annual alcohol-duty uprating that has lifted D7BV +1.3% to +2.7% m/m in ten of ten Januaries, and the annual CPI re-weighting all land in the JANUARY index published 2027-02-17, not in this one. Tiered LOW on the same grounds as every sibling UK CPI entry: symbols: [], no UK listing, no gilt or sterling leg, and no rates- or FX-keyed house playbook.
